explanation: In day1, amount equals quantity * unit_price expressed in dollars with 2 decimals (e.g. row 1000: 2 * 483.94 = 967.88). In day2, amount is exactly 100x larger with no decimal point (e.g. row 2000: 1 * 700.10 -> 70010; row 2007: 8 * 821.93 = 6575.44 -> 657544). The ratio amount / (quantity * unit_price) = 100 for every day2 row, meaning the amount column silently switched from dollars to integer cents (also a float->int type change). unit_price is still in dollars, so the two monetary columns are now on inconsistent scales. All values remain valid numbers with no nulls or parse errors, so ingestion will not fail; downstream revenue sums, average order value, and margin/discount metrics will be inflated 100x without any error. All other columns (order_id sequence advance, customer_id, order_date, status enum, quantity, unit_price format, email with sporadic blanks, discount_pct) are unchanged.
